grounding.cite: According to the disposition sheet I read earlier, which of these stock items should I throw away?

design.premise: During grocery opening, the wearer reads a formal returns disposition sheet: 'DISCARD: DAIRY | HOLD: PRODUCE | KEEP: DRY'. They then walk to another stock surface and inspect an apple and a cereal box while checking the produce and dry-goods inventory. After that natural interruption, they move to the dairy stock counter and inspect a carton of milk and swiss cheese. At turn zero they ask which stock items should be thrown away under the earlier sheet. The assistant remembers the category rule, selects the milk and cheese as dairy, and tells the wearer to discard those two while leaving the produce and dry goods out.

interaction.public_task_context: Apply the earlier disposition rule to the subsequently inspected stock and independently identify the complete set of items the person should discard. Then direct the person one physical step at a time to put only those selected stock items into the public trash can, finishing one item before starting the next and leaving every unselected item on its original stock surface.

invention.author_prose: During grocery opening, the wearer reads a formal returns disposition sheet: 'DISCARD: DAIRY | HOLD: PRODUCE | KEEP: DRY'. They then walk to another stock surface and inspect an apple and a cereal box while checking the produce and dry-goods inventory. After that natural interruption, they move to the dairy stock counter and inspect a carton of milk and swiss cheese. At turn zero they ask which stock items should be thrown away under the earlier sheet. capability.boundary: Use the current view, not episodic memory. The challenge is targeted extraction, not applying specialist knowledge or sorting a large batch.
capability.few_shot: At a shipping desk, three parcels wait on a fixed sorting table. Each label has several nearby fields: order number, customer code, carrier, and outbound dock. With one hand holding a scanner, the wearer asks, 'Which parcel says outbound dock B?' The assistant explicitly inspects the labels, extracts only the dock field, and identifies the matching parcel without confusing dock B with a customer code that also contains B. The wearer places that parcel in the fixed dock-B outbound cage and leaves the two decoys on the table. The final containment relation exposes the answer. This is a current-frame reading task: no earlier glimpse, hidden document, specialist safety advice, or unrelated cleanup is needed.
capability.target: Read a visible label, instruction, sign, or display and extract only the field needed to answer the wearer's question. Distractor fields on the same text must make whole-label paraphrase insufficient.

cast.restaged_story: During grocery opening, the wearer reads a formal returns disposition sheet: 'DISCARD: DAIRY | HOLD: PRODUCE | KEEP: DRY'. They then walk to another stock surface and inspect an apple and a cereal box while checking the produce and dry-goods inventory. After that natural interruption, they move to the dairy stock counter and inspect a carton of milk and swiss cheese. At turn zero they ask which stock items should be thrown away under the earlier sheet. The assistant remembers the category rule, selects the milk and cheese as dairy, and tells the wearer to discard those two while leaving the produce and dry goods out.
cast.why_scene: Provides store counters and trash disposal.

assessment_contract.core_question: According to the disposition sheet I read earlier, which of these stock items should I throw away?
forbidden_changes: Removing the produce and dry-goods distractors
knowledge_constraints: The assistant must remember the read disposition rule after the non-dairy stock-inspection gap.
The assistant must classify visible stock items by category, not by position.
required_evidence: The returns disposition sheet says 'DISCARD: DAIRY | HOLD: PRODUCE | KEEP: DRY'.
The wearer checks an apple in the produce stock after reading the sheet.
The wearer checks a cereal box in the dry-goods stock.
The next stock counter includes a carton of milk.
The next stock counter includes swiss cheese.
The produce and dry-goods inspection separates the earlier rule from the dairy stock decision.
The wearer asks which stock items should be discarded under the note's category rule.
The discard category is dairy.
The milk and cheese are dairy stock items.
The apple and cereal are not dairy items to discard.
temporal_constraints: The wearer reads the rule before inspecting the produce and dry-goods stock.
The wearer observes both stock surfaces before asking which items to discard.
